title: Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon 2026 Review: What the 33rd Edition Was Like
seo_title: Pattaya Marathon 2026 Review: The 33rd Edition | Thailand
meta_description: Pattaya Marathon 2026 review: the 33rd edition ran over 26-27 September in the rain. What the race is like, and what to know before entering next year.
dek: Pattaya's marathon, run since 1993, held its 33rd edition over the weekend of 26 and 27 September 2026, starting in the rain. Here is what the race is like, from what has been published about it.
verdict: The Pattaya Marathon has been run since 1993. The 2026 edition was its 33rd, and it is a World Athletics International Standard Road Race [1]. The 2025 race drew 20,250 entrants across its five categories [1], and the 2026 weekend opened in rain and filled the city with runners and spectators [2][3]. Expect a big, well-established race on a course the organisers themselves call challenging: heat, rolling sections on the Sukhumvit highway and wind on the Jomtien beachfront [1]. It is a good choice if you want a big-city atmosphere at the seaside. Just don't treat it as a fast course.

sections.heading: The 2026 Edition
paragraphs: The 33rd Amazing Thailand Pattaya Marathon ran over the weekend of 26 and 27 September 2026 [2][3]. The Pattaya News reported that it began in rain, with city officials joining the runners [2], and that the weekend drew tens of thousands of people as the city pushed sport tourism [3].

The race is organised by Thailand Tri-League and is held each year on the fourth Sunday of September [1]. Its size is on record: the 2025 event attracted 20,250 entrants across all categories [1]. The organiser describes it as the most popular mass-participation event in the city [1].

sections.heading: Five Categories, One Hard Course
paragraphs: There are five categories: the full marathon, the half marathon, a 10 km, a 4.5 km wheelchair race and a 4.5 km family run [1]. Total prize money of THB 0.76 million is shared across five distances [1] so there is something to race for at the front.

The organisers do not oversell the course. They say runners should be ready for heat on flat and rolling roads along the Sukhumvit highway, wind on Jomtien Beach Road, and a run along Pattaya Beach Road through the tourist centre [1]. A late-September race by the Gulf of Thailand is hot and humid, and in 2026 it was also wet [2]. Plan for conditions, not a personal best.

sections.heading: Should You Enter Next Year?
paragraphs: If you want a large, long-established marathon with a seaside route and an easy trip from Bangkok, yes. Thirty-three editions, World Athletics standard status and a field in the tens of thousands [1][3] add up to an event that knows how to close roads and look after a crowd.
Pick your distance with the weather in mind. The half marathon or 10 km gives you the atmosphere and the beachfront without several hours of September heat.
This review is compiled from the organiser's published information and news reporting on the 2026 race weekend. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: When was the 2026 Pattaya Marathon?
faqs.answer: Over the weekend of Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 September 2026, and it was the 33rd edition of a race first run in 1993. The race is held each year around the fourth Sunday of September, and the 2026 weekend opened in rain, with city officials joining the runners at the start.

faqs.question: How big is the Pattaya Marathon?
faqs.answer: Big. The 2025 event attracted 20,250 entrants across all five categories: the full marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 4.5 km wheelchair race and 4.5 km family run. The 2026 race weekend drew tens of thousands of runners and spectators to the city, and the organiser calls it Pattaya's most popular mass-participation event.

faqs.question: Is the Pattaya Marathon course fast?
faqs.answer: Not especially. The organisers warn of heat on flat and rolling roads along the Sukhumvit highway and wind on Jomtien Beach Road, and the 2026 edition started in rain. Treat it as a hot-weather race.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28, the day after the 2026 race, about that edition. Replaces a pre-race preview. The two Pattaya News reports could not be read in full (the site blocks automated readers), so only what their headlines state is used from them; everything else is from the organiser's own site.
